thread:
maria: Heads-up — we had a near-OOM event in EUW1 (pool-ml-7c) around 06:12 UTC. Several long-chat sessions pushed KV cache memory up and hosts hit memory pressure. Some requests got throttled and retried. Logging it here for a short retro. :warning:

tj: I saw the alerts. Autoscaler started a scale-up but it took ~90s to inject new nodes because of binpacking + a cooldown setting; by the time new capacity came up, kubelet had already started evicting pods. No full crash but lots of 429/503s for ~2m.

leah: Pattern: ~18 sessions with seq lengths >6k tokens, each holding large KV caches. We normally expect 95p <2k, this was an outlier tail plus a promo burst from one customer.

ops-bot: [ALERT 06:12 UTC] cluster/euw1 pool-ml-7c memory_pressure: node/7c-03 evicted pods; autoscaler: scaleUpRequested(3) -> scaleUpInProgress. Fallback applied: routing policy -> model-v1-smaller for new requests.

vikram: Dump from scheduler logs: "FailedScheduling: 0/12 nodes are available: 9 Insufficient memory, 3 node(s) didn't match pod anti-affinity." Looks like anti-affinity rules and our low headroom combined to block quick reschedules.

samir: Quick paste of what I pulled: ```
# kubectl top nodes --selector=pool=pool-ml-7c
NAME         CPU(cores)   CPU%   MEM(bytes)   MEM%
7c-01        3200m        80%    62Gi         88%
7c-02        3100m        78%    61Gi         86%
7c-03        3400m        85%    68Gi         97% <-- pressure
```

sre-oncall: Thanks. Two quick notes: 1) fallback routing prevented more customer-visible errors, good. 2) We still need to avoid the underlying OOM pressure.

leah: Root causes (short list): 1) KV-cache per-session unbounded for very long chats, 2) insufficient headroom in pool to absorb sudden long-tail sessions, 3) autoscaler cooldown + binpack constraints delayed effective scale-up, 4) anti-affinity rules prevented using otherwise idle nodes.

maria: Action items proposal: A) cap KV cache size per session or evict older frames after N tokens, B) increase pool-ml-7c headroom target from 10% -> 25% for EUW1 during promos, C) add burst autoscaler policy with shorter cooldown (30s) and relaxed binpack for emergency scale-ups, D) add alert for per-session memory > 4GB, E) run a chaos test to repro long-chat tail.

tj: Addendum on autoscaler: make a secondary emergency scale path that can ignore anti-affinity and allow some pods on mixed nodes for short windows. We'll gate it behind an annotation so only cluster-admins can trigger.

vikram: Cost note: headroom bump ~+18% GPU hours for EUW1 peak. Recommend we toggle the headroom increase only for 72h surrounding scheduled promos and add a dynamic forecast rule so we don't keep it always.

samir: I'll make a runbook patch: include `kubectl describe node` checks for memory_pressure, and a remediation step to pin high-memory sessions to model-small fallback when node MEM%>90. Also will add the alert dashboard panel.

leah: We should also add a prefetch/forecast job that scans upcoming calendar events and recent usage spikes and auto-creates temporary capacity reservations. Could be part of capacity-forecast pipeline.

maria: Good. Who volunteers to own the follow-ups? I'll take A (KV cache cap) and coordinate with Research for perf regressions. tj take C (autoscaler emergency path) + runbook update with samir. vikram you take B + forecasting toggle and cost estimate. leah you own the chaos test design. sre-oncall will own the postmortem doc and communicate to affected customers with support.

ops-bot: [TASK CREATED] #incidents/1836001234 - owners set: maria, tj, vikram, leah, samir, sre-oncall. ETA initial fixes 72h.

maria: Closing notes: this was mostly a capacity/config gap amplified by an unusual workload tail. Short-term fixes (headroom + emergency autoscaler) will reduce customer impact; medium-term (KV cap + forecasting + chaos tests) to prevent recurrence. Will draft a short postmortem to include ETA and cost impact. :white_check_mark:

tj: I'll post follow-up with exact autoscaler config changes and the cost delta estimate by EOD.

leah: Thanks everyone — good catch on the fallback routing. Learned a lot about our long-chat memory characteristics.
